subject: Licensor boundary and deployment rights — order form redlines
messages:
From: Arielle Myers <arielle.myers@meditech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MSA/Order Form — licensor boundary clarifications

Hi Jordan / Laura,

Thanks for sending the draft. Our legal team flagged a few areas in the MSA and the Order Form where 'licensor' obligations and deployment rights overlap in a way that could expose our on-prem environments. High level:

- Section 5.2 (Deployment Rights) currently reads broad enough that it could be interpreted to allow operator access for troubleshooting. We need explicit limits.
- We are prepared to accept a restricted "snapshot deposit" mechanism, but we need clarity on retention, access method, and whether credentials are included.
- We also want assurance on audit procedures: can a third-party auditor validate the snapshot, or do you require Redwood personnel?

I attached our initial markup to illustrate requested edits. Can Redwood propose language that preserves your ability to validate a private deployment without requiring ongoing operator credentials?

Attachments: MSA_addendum_markup.docx [Attachment: MSA_addendum_markup.docx (docx)]

Thanks,
Arielle Myers
Head of Procurement, MediTech Systems
arielle.myers@meditech.com
+1 415-555-0132

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Myers <arielle.myers@meditech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA/Order Form — licensor boundary clarifications

Hi Arielle — thanks for the clear notes and the markup. Looping in Laura (legal) and David/Priyom (deployments/procurement) to weigh in.

Quick take from engineering/ops side: we can support a "witness-lite snapshot deposit" approach that doesn't require handing over long-term operator credentials. Key constraints we'd need in writing:

- Scope: Redwood provides an encrypted snapshot (forensic image of runtime and configuration artifacts) strictly for validation of deployment capability — not production data.
- Access method: snapshot delivered to a mutually agreed repository (S3 or secure courier) with documented retrieval steps. No live KMS or credential transfer.
- Retention & purge: 30-day retention with certified deletion confirmation unless an audit is initiated.
- Audit access: third-party auditors allowed, but any on-site validation that requires temporary console access must be timeboxed (e.g., 4-hour window, escorted).

I've uploaded our proposed redlines to the Order Form (see attachment) which narrow the Licensor obligations and add a short exhibit describing the witness-lite flow. If you can confirm whether MediTech insists on 'forensic snapshot + third-party analysis' versus a Redwood-led validation, we can draft precise language.

Quoted for context:
> On Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700, Arielle Myers wrote:
> > Our legal team flagged a few areas in the MSA...
> > Attachments: MSA_addendum_markup.docx

- Legal-to-legal sync (30 min) to agree boundary language — can your team do Wed 7/14 16:00 PT?
- If agreed, we prepare a narrow addendum (DocuSign-ready) and route to procurement.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@meditech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: MediTech Legal <legal@meditech.com>, Arielle Myers <arielle.myers@meditech.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA/Order Form — licensor boundary clarifications

Jordan — thanks for the quick reply. Couple clarifications from our legal/engineering side:

- MediTech's position is that Section 5.2 should include an option for an ‘on-prem snapshot deposit’ when required by regulators. That snapshot must be sufficient for a third-party to validate the runtime and model residency.
- We will accept the "witness-lite" model only if Redwood agrees to provide a documented validation checklist and allows a one-time temporary operator access (one-hour session) for the third-party auditor.
- Retention: 45 days preferred; if 30 is the Redwood standard we may accept 30 with an option to extend to 45 upon written request and justification.

We packaged our example exhibit and a zipped set of test artifacts to show the auditor scope. Please review and confirm whether Redwood can accept third-party auditors without KMS-level access (i.e., auditors analyze a sealed snapshot).

Attachments: privdeploy-draft-exhibit.zip [Attachment: privdeploy-draft-exhibit.zip (zip)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@meditech.com>, Arielle Myers <arielle.myers@meditech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA/Order Form — licensor boundary clarifications

Tom / Arielle — appreciate the detail. Summary and concrete next steps from Redwood's side:

1) We can accept sealed snapshot delivery for third-party auditors. Redwood will not provide long-term operator credentials or KMS keys. Auditors will perform analysis against a sealed image and return a signed findings report.
2) Retention: we agree to 30 days as a default with a documented extension process to 45 days upon formal request and approval. We'll add the extension flow to the exhibit.
3) Temporary on-site/console access: Redwood will consider a strictly timeboxed, escorted session limited to verification tasks only. Any session requires an NDA addendum and an operations witness.

Proposed timeline:
- Legal redline exchange: Redwood to provide MSA addendum draft by EOD Fri 2026-07-16.
- Legal sync: Wed 2026-07-14 16:00 PT (30 min) — confirm if that works for your counsel.
- If agreed, we will generate a DocuSign addendum (powerform link below) for signatures.

Proposed language snippet to include in the exhibit:
"Redwood will deliver a sealed, encrypted snapshot of the runtime and configuration artifacts for the sole purpose of independent validation. Redwood will not disclose production credentials or KMS master keys. Access to live systems for auditor-led validation will be limited to a single, escorted session not to exceed four (4) hours, subject to prior written approval and execution of a mutually agreeable confidentiality and operations witness agreement."
